hostCode.behaviour: A file ending in `.xml` or `.xsd` opens in the XML editor.
A file is opened as UTF-8 with or without a byte-order mark, or ASCII, and refused with a reason above 5 MB (before a byte is read), when it looks binary, or when it is not UTF-8.
Every line keeps its own line ending, a new line takes the dominant one, a last line keeps whether it had an ending, and the byte-order mark is written back only when the file had one.
A buffer with one cursor and a selection; Tab writes four spaces; pasted text has its CRLF made LF.
Undo and redo grouped word by word.
hostCode.reason: How typed text is grouped into steps of undo is the host's undo stack (ATD §17).

hostCode.behaviour: Typed text, the movements by character, word, line and document, copy, cut and paste, mapped from keys and the pointer.
hostCode.reason: Which keys and pointer movements edit the text is the host's (ATD §17).

hostCode.behaviour: A line-number gutter, the current line marked, no soft wrap.
Findings drawn as squiggles under their range, coloured by severity.
hostCode.reason: How a finding is drawn is the host's rendering (ATD §17); its severity and place are the description's.

hostCode.behaviour: Findings listed in the problems panel at their line and column, both from 1, columns counted in characters.
Colouring by the token classes of the xml syntax (syntect's Sublime syntaxes), none above 20,000 lines.
The text is read to its end or its first error, one error where the reader stopped, after which the status says "Not well-formed: the rest was not checked."
A DTD or an external entity the reader would have to follow and may not (outside the project, on the web, missing) stops the reading, said as information.
An encoding declared other than the one the file is stored in is a warning, unless every character is ASCII.

The schemas are named by `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation`, the pairs of `xsi:schemaLocation` and the `DOCTYPE`'s system identifier, in the prolog and the root's start tag only, each resolved by the JSON editor's project-only rules.
The document is checked against every XSD it names together, by libxml2.
Without an XSD, a document with a `DOCTYPE` is checked against its DTD.
A root `xs:schema` makes the document a schema, compiled.
A schema that declares XSD 1.1 is said as not supported.
An `xml-model` instruction is named and not supported.

Each of libxml2's findings is said in the sentence and at the place the standalone host's validator gives it: on the element's name, on the value that does not fit, or on the child that is not allowed.
